stem.en: Vinegar contains 5 % v/v acetic acid. Glacial acetic acid is a liquid that is 100 % acetic acid. How do you make 100 mL of vinegar from it?

text.en: Measure 5 mL of glacial acetic acid and add 100 mL of water.
Measure 5 mL of glacial acetic acid and add water until the total is 100 mL.
Weigh 5 g of glacial acetic acid and add water until the total is 100 g.
Measure 95 mL of glacial acetic acid and add 5 mL of water.

explanation.en: 5 % v/v means 5 mL of acid in every 100 mL of solution, so the total must be 100 mL. Option a is the common mistake: it gives 105 mL, because 100 mL of water is added to the 5 mL of acid. Option c measures by mass, but the label says v/v. Option d swaps the two parts and would make 95 % acid.

hints.en: What do the letters v/v tell you to measure?
100 mL is the total volume, not the volume of water.
